title: Voice-input for the worksheet brief
summary: Web Speech API integration on the natural-language input panel. A 'Speak your brief' button records → transcribes → drops into the existing parseNaturalLanguageInput parser at ai.ts §NL-PARSE. No new server route. Pure frontend; degrades gracefully where Web Speech API isn't supported.

in: client/src/hooks/useVoiceToText.tsx — there's already a useVoiceToText helper in Worksheets.tsx §HOOK-VOICE; either factor it out into client/src/hooks/ or reuse in place
client/src/components/VoiceBriefButton.tsx (new, ~80 LoC) — button + recording-state UI (idle / recording / transcribing / done) + permission-denied fallback
client/src/pages/Worksheets.tsx — wire VoiceBriefButton into the natural-language input panel; on transcription, call parseNaturalLanguageInput
Targeted vitest: state machine transitions; permission-denied handled; transcript correctly fed to parser
out: Server-side transcription (Whisper API) — deferred; v1 uses the browser-native Web Speech API which is free and respects user privacy
Multi-language voice input (deferred — Web Speech API supports it but localisation is Phase H's H3 territory)

acceptance_criteria: Button toggles recording on click; visual feedback during recording.
Transcript is fed to parseNaturalLanguageInput which sets the form state via the existing flow.
Permission-denied surfaces a clear 'Microphone access required' message with a 'How to enable' link.
Falls back to typed input if Web Speech API is unsupported.

risk_register.risk: Web Speech API is browser-dependent (Chrome/Edge support; Firefox partial; Safari limited)
risk_register.mitigation: Detect support at mount; hide the button when unsupported; show typed-input only.

risk_register.risk: Transcription accuracy on UK accents / SEND voices
risk_register.mitigation: Web Speech API is sufficient for v1; if accuracy is poor we can swap in Whisper server-side later behind an env flag.

related: G3 — lesson archetypes (voice input could populate the archetype picker too)
